subject: English
passage:
The following text is adapted from Imran Ito's 1908 essay on art criticism, A Question of Attribution.

If I am not mistaken, 'tis the obligation of a critic to present every painting under its true provenance, and to record an attribution upon its rightful evidence, and upon no other: I mean by this, (for I would be as plain as I am able) that where a canvas is assigned to a master with credible documentation, he ought to lay before the public the particular proof of its origin, or else he is not faithful to the work; and where it comes without such documentation, he ought to declare as much, lest he prove unfaithful to himself.
prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Because no attribution can be verified, all critics must concede that some catalogues of paintings are, in part, mistaken.
choices.B: The only paintings a critic should write about are those whose authorship has been established beyond dispute.
choices.C: It is hard for critics to be entirely accurate in matters of attribution, and in time they will regret some of their judgments.
choices.D: Critics should clearly indicate the extent to which the attribution of each painting is supported by evidence.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer. The text lays out what Ito believes is the duty of an art critic: when a painting is assigned to a master with credible documentation, the critic should present the particular proof; when it comes without such documentation, the critic should say so. In other words, critics should clearly indicate the extent to which each attribution is supported by evidence.
